title: Java News Roundup: TornadoVM, A2A Java, Open Liberty, Open J Proxy, Gradle, EclipseStore
gist: InfoQ's weekly Java roundup for November 2, 2026 lists point releases and release candidates across the Java ecosystem, including TornadoVM 8.1.0, A2A Java SDK 1.5.0, Quarkus 4.0 beta 3, Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 and Gradle 9.9.0. The only forward-looking item is the JReleaser 2.0 roadmap with breaking changes.

insights.claim: TornadoInsight 2.1.0, the IntelliJ IDEA plugin for TornadoVM, adds an experimental AI-assisted transformation of a Java method into a TornadoVM kernel.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: AI-assisted code generation is reaching GPU-acceleration tooling in the Java ecosystem.
insights.locator: Beehive Lab has also released version 2.1.0

insights.claim: A2A Java SDK 1.5.0 implements the Agent2Agent Protocol for running agentic applications as A2AServers and adds OpenTelemetry push-notification instrumentation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Agent interoperability protocols are gaining first-class Java support.

insights.claim: TornadoVM 8.1.0 lets a kernel read and write a device allocation owned by another library in place, without copying it.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Zero-copy interop eases GPU workload integration from Java.

insights.claim: Quarkus 4.0.0 third beta adds Valkey support in the Quarkus Redis Client extension.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Valkey support shows Redis-fork adoption in mainstream Java frameworks.

insights.claim: Open Liberty 26.0.0.11 resolves numerous CVEs, makes the previously fixed 30-second server quiesce timeout configurable, and blocks form-login redirects to external hosts unless listed.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Routine security hardening in enterprise Java runtimes.

insights.claim: Gradle 9.9.0 enables incremental compilation of Kotlin DSL scripts via the Kotlin Build Tools API for improved build performance.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Build performance gains reduce developer cycle time.

insights.claim: EclipseStore 4.3.0 refactors the VectorIndex interface in its JVector Index for large indices, concurrent load and crash safety, and deprecates the standalone Vaadin/Spring-based client GUI.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Vector indexing is being built into Java-native storage.

insights.claim: The JReleaser 2.0 roadmap requires a minimum of JDK 25 and Gradle 9+, removes all deprecations and drops OSX Intel artifact support, with numerous breaking changes expected over the coming weeks.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Signals the Java toolchain moving off Intel macOS and older JDKs.
